about: Cited adaptation solutions for the hazards the twin actually shows for pea: drought at flowering (H1) and heat at flowering (H2). Every quote was read in the source on 2026-11-08 (verbatim, short). Nothing here is reviewed by a person yet: reviewed_by stays null until a human signs it off. The yield model can run some of these (lever); the rest are evidence only, never simulated numbers.

solutions.title: Water the peas at flowering, not all season
solutions.what: Plan supplementary irrigation for the flowering weeks (June in both regions), when a dry spell costs the most pods.
solutions.lead_time: same season if equipment and water exist
solutions.limits: Summer water may not be there when it is needed most, especially in south-east Sweden.

evidence.quote: the drought sensitivity of pea was high during the flowering phase … and considerably lower during the pod filling phase
The yield loss was mainly the result of a lower number of pods per stalk.

evidence.locator: §5.5, Bevattning i dag och i framtiden
evidence.quote: Tillgången på ytvatten för bevattning kan komma att bli mycket begränsad i vissa områden under den period då vattenbehovet är som störst.
evidence.translation: Surface water for irrigation may become very limited in some areas just when the need is greatest.

solutions.title: Store water before summer: ponds and wetlands
solutions.what: Build or restore irrigation ponds and wetlands with neighbours, so water caught in winter and spring is there for June.
solutions.limits: Needs local planning and permits; county grants exist but are not guaranteed.

evidence.locator: p. 2, Våtmarker eller bevattningsdammar i odlingslandskapet
evidence.quote: kan du reglera vattenflöden och magasinera vatten inför torra perioder
evidence.translation: you can regulate water flows and store water ahead of dry periods

evidence.locator: §5.5, Bevattning i dag och i framtiden
evidence.quote: I framtiden kommer torka bli ett större problem under sommaren, framför allt i östra och sydöstra Sverige
evidence.translation: In future, drought will become a bigger problem in summer, above all in eastern and south-eastern Sweden

solutions.title: Keep more water in the soil: reduced tillage and cover crops
solutions.what: Move towards reduced or no tillage and keep the soil covered, so it holds more of the spring rain into the dry weeks.
solutions.lead_time: about a year to start; soil benefits build over several seasons
solutions.limits: Possible short-term yield dip while switching; machinery can be costly for small farms.

evidence.quote: can protect the soil from erosion, retain moisture, suppress weeds and pests, and improve biodiversity and soil structure
Possible short-term yield reductions during the transition period.

evidence.locator: p. 3, Ett variationsrikt landskap och en mångfald av grödor
evidence.quote: använda olika typer av täckgrödor för att minska avdunstning från jorden vid torka
evidence.translation: use different kinds of cover crops to reduce evaporation from the soil in drought

solutions.title: Sow earlier so peas flower before the summer stress
solutions.what: Use the earlier spring to sow peas sooner, moving flowering ahead of the hottest and driest weeks.
solutions.limits: Cold, wet soils in early spring can hurt emergence; the gain depends on the year.

evidence.locator: §5.1.4 Förändrade förutsättningar för jordbruk och trädgårdsodling
evidence.quote: Den största skillnaden blir då främst tidigare start på vegetationsperioden i södra och sydvästra Sverige.
evidence.translation: The biggest change is above all an earlier start of the growing season in southern and south-western Sweden.

evidence.quote: the production declines when the maximum day temperature during flowering exceeds 25°C

solutions.title: Grow heat-resistant pea types: upright, semi-leafless cultivars
solutions.what: Prefer upright, semi-leafless cultivars that stay cooler and set more pods in heat, and trial new heat-tolerant lines with breeders.
solutions.lead_time: 1 year to switch cultivar; years for new breeding lines
solutions.limits: The model's heat-tolerant pea effect is an assumption, not measured; trials are needed before relying on it.

evidence.quote: semileafless cultivars with the upright habit had cooler canopies and greater seed yield, pod number and pod to node ratio than normal leafed vining cultivars
the impact of HSEs is more prominent on the RP than the vegetative period
One year is needed to change cultivated varieties of annual crops and obtain the production

solutions.title: Spread the risk: several varieties and both regions
solutions.what: Contract a mix of pea varieties and keep volume in both SW Finland and Skåne, so one bad June does not hit everything.
solutions.limits: Spreading lowers the worst year but not the average weather risk.

evidence.locator: p. 3, Ett variationsrikt landskap och en mångfald av grödor
evidence.quote: Genom att ha ett diversifierat jordbruk sprider du riskerna mellan olika typer av grödor
evidence.translation: With diversified farming you spread the risks across different kinds of crops

evidence.quote: Diversifying crops and selecting climate resilient varieties strengthen the ability of the agro-ecosystem
